questions.text: Production in economics is BEST defined as:
options: B) Transformation of inputs into outputs
C) Buying and selling of goods
questions.correct_answer: B) Transformation of inputs into outputs
questions.explanation: Production is the process of transforming INPUTS (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) into OUTPUTS (goods and services). It's NOT just manufacturing — services like teaching, healthcare, and transportation are also production. Any activity that creates value or utility is production.

questions.text: In the SHORT RUN, which of the following is TRUE?
options: B) At least one input is fixed
questions.correct_answer: B) At least one input is fixed
questions.explanation: The SHORT RUN is defined as the period where at least ONE input is FIXED (usually capital like machinery, buildings). Firms can only vary some inputs (like labor). In the LONG RUN, ALL inputs are variable. Example: A bakery can't build a new oven overnight (fixed) but can hire more workers (variable).

questions.text: The production function Q = f(L, K) shows:
options: A) The relationship between price and quantity
B) The technical relationship between inputs and maximum output
C) The financial relationship between costs and revenue
D) The marketing relationship between advertising and sales
questions.correct_answer: B) The technical relationship between inputs and maximum output
questions.explanation: The production function Q = f(L, K) shows the TECHNICAL relationship between inputs (L = Labor, K = Capital) and the MAXIMUM output (Q) that can be produced. It's 'technical' because it's about physical quantities, not prices or money. It assumes efficient production with given technology.

questions.text: Examine the production table below. What is the Marginal Product of the 4th worker?
questions.diagram: <svg width='320' height='200' viewBox='0 0 320 200'><rect width='320' height='200' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><text x='160' y='25' text-anchor='middle' fill='#f59e0b' font-size='13' font-weight='bold'>Production Schedule</text><rect x='50' y='40' width='220' height='130' fill='#1a2332' rx='4'/><text x='70' y='60' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>Workers (L)</text><text x='150' y='60' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>TP (Q)</text><text x='220' y='60' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>MP</text><line x1='50' y1='70' x2='270' y2='70' stroke='#334155' stroke-width='1'/><text x='70' y='90' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>1</text><text x='150' y='90' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>10</text><text x='220' y='90' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>10</text><text x='70' y='115' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>2</text><text x='150' y='115' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>25</text><text x='220' y='115' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>15</text><text x='70' y='140' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>3</text><text x='150' y='140' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>45</text><text x='220' y='140' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>20</text><text x='70' y='165' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>4</text><text x='150' y='165' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>60</text><text x='220' y='165' fill='#f8fafc' font-size='11'>?</text></svg>
questions.explanation: Marginal Product = Change in TP / Change in L. MP of 4th worker = TP(4) - TP(3) = 60 - 45 = 15. The 4th worker adds 15 units to total production. MP measures the ADDITIONAL output from one MORE worker.

questions.text: If Total Product is 100 when L = 5, what is the Average Product?
questions.explanation: Average Product = Total Product / Labor = 100 / 5 = 20 units per worker. AP measures the OUTPUT PER WORKER — how productive each worker is on average.

questions.text: The Law of Variable Proportions (Diminishing Returns) states that:
options: A) Output always increases with more workers
B) Marginal product eventually declines as more variable input is added to fixed input
C) All inputs should be increased equally
D) Production is impossible without capital
questions.correct_answer: B) Marginal product eventually declines as more variable input is added to fixed input
questions.explanation: The Law of Variable Proportions (Diminishing Returns) states that when more units of a VARIABLE input (labor) are added to FIXED inputs (capital), beyond a certain point, the MARGINAL PRODUCT will eventually DECLINE. Example: Adding more workers to a fixed kitchen — eventually they get in each other's way.

questions.text: Examine the diagram below. In which stage is MP NEGATIVE?
questions.diagram: <svg width='350' height='180' viewBox='0 0 350 180'><rect width='350' height='180' fill='#111827' rx='8'/><line x1='40' y1='150' x2='330' y2='150' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='20' x2='40' y2='150' stroke='#38bdf8' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M 40 140 Q 120 20 170 30 Q 230 40 260 130 Q 270 160 280 150' stroke='#facc15' stroke-width='3' fill='none'/><line x1='130' y1='20' x2='130' y2='150' stroke='#64748b' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='3,3'/><text x='90' y='15' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>Stage I</text><line x1='200' y1='20' x2='200' y2='150' stroke='#64748b' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='3,3'/><text x='160' y='15' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>Stage II</text><text x='260' y='15' fill='#94a3b8' font-size='10'>Stage III</text><text x='320' y='165' fill='#38bdf8' font-size='12' font-weight='bold'>L</text></svg>
questions.explanation: In Stage III, Marginal Product is NEGATIVE — adding more workers actually REDUCES total output because there are too many workers and not enough fixed capital. Workers get in each other's way. No rational producer operates in Stage III.

questions.text: The RATIONAL stage of production where a firm should operate is:
options: B) Stage II (MP decreasing but positive)
D) Any stage works equally well
questions.correct_answer: B) Stage II (MP decreasing but positive)
questions.explanation: Stage II is the RATIONAL production zone because: MP is DECREASING but still POSITIVE (TP still increasing). In Stage I, the firm is UNDERUSING its fixed capital (should add more workers). In Stage III, there are TOO MANY workers (TP decreasing). Stage II is where the firm maximizes efficiency.

questions.text: When MP is at its MAXIMUM, what is happening to TP?
options: B) TP is increasing at the fastest rate
questions.correct_answer: B) TP is increasing at the fastest rate
questions.explanation: When MP is at MAXIMUM, TP is increasing at its FASTEST rate (the inflection point). This is where each additional worker adds the MOST to output. After this point, TP continues to increase but at a DECREASING rate (MP declines).

questions.text: If MP = 0, what does this mean for TP?
options: A) TP is at its MAXIMUM
questions.correct_answer: A) TP is at its MAXIMUM
questions.explanation: When MP = 0, adding one more worker doesn't change total output — TP is at its MAXIMUM. This is the boundary between Stage II and Stage III. Beyond this point, MP becomes NEGATIVE and TP starts DECREASING. The firm should NEVER hire workers beyond this point.
